Job Summary

This position can be based in GBSKuala Lumpur or GBS Guangzhou. When prompted, please select your preferred location from the drop down. The recruitment team will contact you to confirm your preferred location if you are shortlisted.

Assurance is a Second line defence function established under a delegated Mandate from the Group Chief Risk Officer and the Group Head of Conduct, Financial Crime and Compliance (CFCR). The primary role of Assurance is to provide a risk-based independent view to Senior Management in the business/functions, Second Line and the Board as to the effectiveness of the bank’s policies, processes, systems and controls. It facilitates identification of any gaps & inefficiencies, enabling prompt corrective action to be taken, and is a key source of evidence for the Board & Regulators. Assurance is part of the reasonable steps taken in support of SMF 4, 16 & 17 responsibilities.

The Director, CFCR Assurance role operates within a globally integrated and fungible operating model, working closely with others in the CFCR Assurance team to focus on delivery of Assurance reviews within the CFCR Assurance remit.

Key Responsibilities

Strategy

  • Support the Co-Lead, CFCR Assurance in delivering a strategy for risk-based and data-enabled assurance coverage across CFCR Assurance, aligned to the Bank’s risk profile, regulatory expectations and internal commitments.
  • Support the agenda to drive a collaborative risk and control ecosystem across the three Lines of Defence, including effective reliance and remediation tracking.
  • Support the agenda to drive a culture of continuous improvement in assurance delivery, including consistent methodology application, strong documentation and evidence standards, and timely reporting and escalation.

Business

  • Provide support on the delivery of the assurance plan and book of work to ensure alignment to CFCR Assurance priorities.
  • Maintain a strong quality culture across planning, fieldwork, reporting and issue validation.
  • Maintain strong awareness of CFCR Assurance regulatory expectations, internal policies/standards, and leading practices in risk management, control testing and assurance.

Processes

  • Work closely with teams across the three Lines of Defence, building good working relationships and engaging with 1LoD testing teams and Risk owners.
  • Follow the Group’s policies and standards, including how we carry out assurance work, track issues, and keep documentation clear and consistent.

People & Talent

  • Promote and embed a culture of openness, trust and risk awareness, where ethical, legal, regulatory and policy compliant conduct is the norm.
  • Take personal responsibility for embedding the highest standards of ethics, including regulatory and business conduct, across the Group. This includes understanding and ensuring compliance with, in letter and spirit, all applicable laws, regulations, guidelines and the Group Code of Conduct.

Risk Management

  • Retesting of controls to support the assessment on both design and operating effectiveness across key processes
  • Support the delivery of a dynamic plan that focuses assurance activity on areas of highest risk and greatest potential impact, including thematic work across geographies where appropriate.
  • Communicate issues and testing insights clearly to senior stakeholders as required, including through concise reporting, escalation and remediation validation

Regulatory & Business Conduct

  • Display exemplary conduct and live by the Group’s Values and Code of Conduct.
  • Take personal responsibility for embedding the highest standards of ethics, including regulatory and business conduct, across Standard Chartered Bank. This includes understanding and ensuring compliance with, in letter and spirit, all applicable laws, regulations, guidelines and the Group Code of Conduct.

Key stakeholders

  • Global Head of Assurance
  • CFCR Assurance Co-leads
  • Globa Head of CFCRs Assurance Management Team
  • Global Head of Assurance’s Management Team
  • Risk Market CROs/CCO
  • Group Internal Audit & Investigations
  • Legal & Group Corporate Secretariat (GCS)
  • COOs and Conduct and Control leads – business and functions
  • 1LOD testing teams
  • Key regulatory bodies (as required) e.g. Bank of England, HKMA, MAS etc.
  • Appointed Regulatory Monitors

Other Responsibilities

  • Embed Here for good and Group’s brand and values in the Global Assurance team.
  • Perform other responsibilities assigned under Group, Country/Market, Business or Functional policies and procedures.
  • Conduct internal investigation in rare circumstances where the both the Shared Investigative Services team and Compliance Speaking-up team are both implicated in an investigation.
  • Execute director responsibilities to entities where appointed as a Director, to ensure effective oversight and governance in line with local laws and the Group’s polices and risk frameworks.

Skills And Experience

  • Risk Specialism
  • Market Expertise
  • Independent Challenge
  • Commercial Mindset
  • Execution - Driven
  • Critical - Thinking
  • Solution Driven
  • Proficiency in Tech, AI/ Automation
  • Managing Change & Conflict
  • Integrity
  • People Leadership
  • Stakeholder management & Influence

Qualifications

  • Strong assurance, risk and control testing, regulatory inspection within a banking environment.
  • Substantial experience in the banking industry, including demonstrated success in a similar roles, including across a range of risk areas.
  • Experience in leading transformations in risk and control testing/audit/assurance.
  • Experience in optimising processes, including via the use of technology.
  • Strong leadership qualities, excellent interpersonal skills and personal authority based on trusted relationships.
  • Experienced in building leading and motivating teams.
  • Strategic vision for the function.
  • Excellent communicator, effective leader and manager of complex, highly matrixed organizations and the ability to explain complex risk terms in business language.
  • Ability to collaborate and work dynamically across country, region, business, and group stakeholders
  • Strong drive, high levels of integrity, independence, and enthusiasm.
  • Strong expertise in data analytics, AI, automation, and technology risk management in banking.
  • Strong presentation skills and the overall knowledge, sound judgement and courage of conviction.

About Standard Chartered

We're an international bank, nimble enough to act, big enough for impact. For more than 170 years, we've worked to make a positive difference for our clients, communities, and each other. We question the status quo, love a challenge and enjoy finding new opportunities to grow and do better than before. If you're looking for a career with purpose and you want to work for a bank making a difference, we want to hear from you. You can count on us to celebrate your unique talents and we can't wait to see the talents you can bring us.

Our purpose, to drive commerce and prosperity through our unique diversity, together with our brand promise, to be here for good are achieved by how we each live our valued behaviours. When you work with us, you'll see how we value difference and advocate inclusion.

Together We

  • Do the right thing and are assertive, challenge one another, and live with integrity, while putting the client at the heart of what we do
  • Never settle, continuously striving to improve and innovate, keeping things simple and learning from doing well, and not so well
  • Are better together, we can be ourselves, be inclusive, see more good in others, and work collectively to build for the long term

What We Offer

In line with our Fair Pay Charter, we offer a competitive salary and benefits to support your mental, physical, financial and social wellbeing.

  • Core bank funding for retirement savings, medical and life insurance, with flexible and voluntary benefits available in some locations.
  • Time-off including annual leave, parental/maternity (20 weeks), sabbatical (12 months maximum) and volunteering leave (3 days), along with minimum global standards for annual and public holiday, which is combined to 30 days minimum.
  • Flexible working options based around home and office locations, with flexible working patterns.
  • Proactive wellbeing support through Unmind, a market-leading digital wellbeing platform, development courses for resilience and other human skills, global Employee Assistance Programme, sick leave, mental health first-aiders and all sorts of self-help toolkits
  • A continuous learning culture to support your growth, with opportunities to reskill and upskill and access to physical, virtual and digital learning.
  • Being part of an inclusive and values driven organisation, one that embraces and celebrates our unique diversity, across our teams, business functions and geographies - everyone feels respected and can realise their full potential.

We are currently seeking an experienced professional to join our team in the role of Senior Consultant Specialist.

Business: Asia & Middle East Technology

Job ID:48755

Principal Responsibilities

Requirements gathering & stakeholder partnering

  • Run structured discovery sessions with business users to understand reporting needs, decision journeys, KPIs, and pain points.
  • Translate user needs into clear functional requirements, user stories, acceptance criteria, and dashboard wireframes.
  • Manage stakeholder expectations, prioritisation, and delivery timelines across multiple teams.

Critical report development across visualisation tools

  • Design and develop executive-ready dashboards and operational reports using tools such as Superset, Tableau (and others as required).
  • Apply strong data visualisation principles (clarity, accessibility, performance, and narrative) to deliver actionable insights.
  • Ensure reports are accurate, reconciled, and aligned to agreed definitions and data sources.

Migration leadership (Tableau → Superset)

  • Own and drive the end-to-end migration of existing reports to Superset, including assessment, redesign where needed, rebuild, testing, and cutover.
  • Create migration playbooks, templates, and repeatable approaches to accelerate delivery and reduce risk.
  • Partner with data engineering/platform teams to resolve data model, performance, and access considerations.

Reporting standards & strategy

  • Define and maintain reporting standards (layout, KPI definitions, naming conventions, certification, documentation, and governance).
  • Establish best practices for dashboard performance, usability, and lifecycle management (build, publish, change control, decommission).
  • Contribute to the broader reporting strategy and roadmap, including tool adoption and rationalisation.

User enablement & self-service support

  • Coach users on self-service dashboard development and best practices in Superset (and other tools where relevant).
  • Produce user guides, training materials, and “how-to” sessions to uplift capability across the community.
  • Provide advisory support and troubleshooting to help users deliver their own reporting safely and efficiently.

Requirements

  • Strong hands-on experience delivering dashboards and reports
  • Proven track record in requirements gathering, stakeholder management, and translating business needs into effective visual solutions.
  • Experience leading or contributing to report migration or tool transition programmes.
  • Solid understanding of data concepts: datasets, semantic layers, metrics/KPIs, data quality, and reconciliation.
  • Strong communication skills—able to explain complex data topics to non-technical audiences and influence outcomes.

Job Summary

  • This is a role within the Risk function to support work performed by the Enterprise Risk Management team. Key tasks include ensuring central elements of Hong Kong’s risk governance and control framework are operating effectively, within risk appetite and in line with internal frameworks and policies as well as statutory and regulatory requirements.

Strategy

  • Awareness and understanding of the Group’s business strategy and model, supporting the identification of emerging risks.
  • Maintain good level of understanding of the latest regulatory requirements which are of relevance to the Risk function.

Business

  • Awareness and understanding of the wider business, economic and market environment in which the Group operates.
  • Being a trusted Risk partner to the Business and effectively challenge where needed.

Processes

  • Support the Risk Function in the management of risk appetite for Greater China and North Asia (“GCNA”) region.
  • Support the implementation and maintenance of the Enterprise Risk Management Framework across relevant entities in GCNA region.
  • Support BCBS239 compliance for GCNA.
  • Support the Risk Function in the management of large exposure and country risk.
  • Support the timely delivery and submission of dashboards, presentation materials, committee papers, etc.
  • Support relevant Risk teams in the management of regulatory examination as appropriate.

People & Talent

  • Self-disciplined and pro-actively lead enterprise risk management initiatives across the GCNA region.
  • Strong collaboration skills to partner with various stakeholders across the Group.

Risk Management

  • The key responsibility for the role is to lead the implementation of Enterprise Risk Management initiatives for the GCNA region, including
  • Guide the GCNA region on adoption of Enterprise Risk Management Framework and respective Risk Type Framework;
  • Support the policy governance for the GCNA region; and
  • Continued enhancement and introduction of new initiatives and supporting enterprise risk management activities for the GCNA region.
  • Be the principal point of contact and support the Chief Risk Officer in discharging regional oversight responsibilities in relation to Reputational & Sustainability Risks, Country Risk, Climate Risk, and Strategic Risk. This include enhancing and implementation of the relevant risk frameworks, ownership of regulatory rules, monitoring of risk and reporting as appropriate.

Governance

  • Lead the monitoring and management of large exposure and country risk exposure.
  • Prepare/collate papers, information packs and presentations as required by the CRO for Risk governance meetings and Board Meetings as required.
  • Track and escalate issues and undertake follow-up actions as required.

Regulatory & Business Conduct

  • Display exemplary conduct and live by the Group’s Values and Code of Conduct.
  • Take personal responsibility for embedding the highest standards of ethics, including regulatory and business conduct, across Standard Chartered Bank. This includes understanding and ensuring compliance with, in letter and spirit, all applicable laws, regulations, guidelines and the Group Code of Conduct.
  • Effectively and collaboratively identify, escalate, mitigate and resolve risk, conduct and compliance matters.

Key stakeholders

  • Chief Risk Officer, Risk Function, Business, Group Risk, GCNA Risk teams, GBS teams

Other Responsibilities

  • Embed Here for good and Group’s brand and values in HK & GCNA ERM; Perform other responsibilities assigned under Group, Country, Business or Functional policies and procedures.

Qualifications

  • Educated to degree level.
  • Broad experience in Banking industry with minimum of 5 years’ experience, risk management experience preferred.
  • Knowledge and understanding of regulatory requirements, namely those from the HKMA, PRA and Basel.
  • Prior experience in Finance/Risk/Compliance/Audit/Governance.
  • Excellent written and spoken English, with additional ability in Chinese (Cantonese and/or Mandarin) a bonus.
  • Very strong communication skills (both written and verbal), with the ability to interact confidently with senior stakeholders
  • Ability to manage multiple tasks successfully and efficiently in a fast paced, regulatory driven environment.
  • Strong analytical, conceptualisation and independent thinking skills

Skill And Experiences

  • Communication (verbal and written)
  • Influencing stakeholders
  • Manage multiple tasks
  • Analytical thinking
  • Change driver
  • Problem solving

We're an international bank, nimble enough to act, big enough for impact. For more than 170 years, we've worked to make a positive difference for our clients, communities, and each other. Position Purpose

The job purpose is to partner directly with the head of 2S China, ensuring the business operates safely and complies with all internal BNP Paribas Group rules as well as Regulations in China.

He/She will manage directly the Operations team (namely Client Delivery), act as local contact for Global Process Owners and Client Lines representatives. Finally, he/she will act as a delegate for the head of 2S China (as required) and roll-out locally global initiatives: efficiency, rationalization, digitalization.

Direct Responsibilities

  • Ensure the team provide an excellent, efficient and consistent service delivery to clients, in cooperation with Client Services.
  • Act as escalation point for service delivery issues within the location & ensure a proper escalation to Client Services when needed.
  • Drive the local business delivery model by aligning local operational resources to global standards as well as global development plans and priorities (incl. but not limited to Business Implementation team).
  • Define & monitor service quality metrics and articulate action plans to improve service quality.
  • Minimise the operational risk and ensure the local business continuity plan is available & tested.
  • Implement new product capabilities as per Client Lines roadmap
  • Respond to local authority’s requirements and ensure business delivery model is compliant with local obligations.
  • Manage client delivery costs in the location with the objective to minimise the cost base, monitor the evolution of unit costs, review and validate local budget targets.
  • Responsible for the implementation of operational permanent control policies and procedures in day-to-day business activities, such as Control Plan (work closely with LoD1 in that regards).
  • Responsible for ensuring team members to comply with regulatory requirements and internal guidelines, full adhesion to Compliance, Conduct & Risk policies.
  • Responsible for reporting all incidents according to the Incident Management System.
  • Responsible for ensuring job descriptions are written, distributed and updated.

Contributing Responsibilities

  • Contribute as Settlement Officer and provide high-quality service to clients in a secure operating environment.
  • Support sales and product forces by acting as an expert of local business delivery model (RFP participation, etc.)
  • Contribute to feasibility assessment on new product capabilities.
  • Actively participate to local marketplace committees and ensure appropriate internal reporting.

Job Type

Job Reference #

336879BR

City

Shanghai

Key Responsibilities

Do you like financial markets? Are you good at handling and interpreting large data sets? Are you analytical and enjoy investigating financial transactions, understanding trading strategies and making sense of the unusual trading activity?

We are seeking an experienced Market Conduct Surveillance Analyst with deep practitioner experience, capable of operating with a high degree of independence while remaining fully embedded within an integrated regional surveillance framework. In this role, you will:

  • Perform end‑to‑end trade surveillance activities across the Investment Bank (IB) and Global Wealth Management (GWM) businesses, with primary accountability for China‑local activity.
  • Independently analyze alerts, exceptions and instances of potentially unusual or suspicious trading activity generated by surveillance systems, forming well‑reasoned conclusions.
  • Apply deep, practical knowledge of China local securities regulations, including Abnormal Trading Rules and Program Trading Rules, when assessing and determining market conduct risk.
  • Leverage a strong understanding of cash equities and related IB & GWM products, execution processes, trading strategies and the end‑to‑end trade lifecycle to support robust and defensible investigations.
  • Act as the primary surveillance authority for China‑local activity, exercising a high degree of independent analysis, judgment and decision‑making in risk assessments and outcomes.
  • Engage directly with front‑office businesses, control functions and regional partners on escalations, inquiries and remediation actions, challenging where appropriate.
  • Represent surveillance function in interactions with exchange surveillance teams and regulators, including responding to inquiries and managing follow‑ups as required.
  • Collaborate closely with colleagues as part of an integrated APAC Market Conduct Surveillance team, actively participating in regional training and knowledge sharing initiatives to promote cross market consistency while addressing China specific market conduct risks.
  • Drive continuous process improvements and contribute to strategic initiatives, automation and optimization projects within the function.
  • Build and maintain effective working relationships with senior management and key stakeholders across the first and second lines of defence in China and across the region, establishing credibility as a trusted subject‑matter expert.

The team

You will be part of the APAC Market Conduct Surveillance team functionally, a second‑line function within Group Compliance and Operational Risk Control, supporting the firm in achieving its strategic, operational and regulatory objectives.

The role is based in Shanghai, with primary accountability for China‑local trade surveillance activities. In addition to day‑to‑day surveillance coverage, the role will play a key part in establishing and further developing the Market Conduct Surveillance operating model in China, aligned with existing APAC governance, standards and escalation frameworks.

While operating with a high degree of independence in line with local regulatory and data‑privacy requirements, the role is fully integrated within the broader APAC regional framework, providing exposure to regional governance, escalation practices and cross‑market regulatory expectations, alongside focused ownership of China‑specific market conduct risks.

Your Skills And Experience

  • Proven hands‑on experience in market conduct and/or trade surveillance within a financial institution or securities regulator.
  • Strong hands‑on experience with automated trade surveillance systems, including scenario design and system configuration, with the ability to independently review, assess and dispose of alerts and to propose enhancements to surveillance coverage where appropriate.
  • Strong knowledge of China securities market regulations, with particular emphasis on Abnormal Trading Rules and Program Trading Rules, and proven ability to apply these rules in both the design and tuning of surveillance scenarios and the independent assessment and disposition of alerts.
  • Demonstrated experience independently handling exchange‑driven surveillance inquiries and regulatory referrals from SSE/SZSE, including analysis, response formulation and follow‑up.
  • Solid understanding of execution processes for cash equities and related instruments, including order handling, execution workflows and post‑trade processes.
  • Strong understanding of trading strategies, market behavior and the end‑to‑end trade lifecycle, enabling meaningful and well‑reasoned analysis of suspicious or unusual trading activity.
  • Strong analytical mindset, with the ability to investigate issues in depth, identify root causes and reach sound, defensible conclusions.
  • Excellent organizational, time‑management, documentation and problem‑solving skills, with a high level of attention to detail.
  • Commitment to staying current on regulatory developments, internal policy changes and evolving market practices.
  • Ability to communicate clearly, confidently and credibly with a broad range of stakeholders, including senior business and compliance stakeholders and regional partners.

About Us
UBS is a leading and truly global wealth manager and the leading universal bank in Switzerland. We also provide diversified asset management solutions and focused investment banking capabilities. Headquartered in Zurich, Switzerland, UBS is present in more than 50 markets around the globe.

We know that great work is never done alone. That’s why we place collaboration at the heart of everything we do. Because together, we’re more than ourselves. Want to find out more? Visit ubs.com/careers.

Join us

At UBS, we know that it's our people, with their diverse skills, experiences and backgrounds, who drive our ongoing success. We’re dedicated to our craft and passionate about putting our people first, with new challenges, a supportive team, opportunities to grow and flexible working options when possible. Our inclusive culture brings out the best in our employees, wherever they are on their career journey. And we use artificial intelligence (AI) to work smarter and more efficiently. We also recognize that great work is never done alone. That’s why collaboration is at the heart of everything we do. Because together, we’re more than ourselves.

We’re committed to disability inclusion and if you need reasonable accommodation/adjustments throughout our recruitment process, you can always contact us.

Contact Details

UBS Recruiting

Disclaimer / Policy statements

UBS is an Equal Opportunity Employer. We respect and seek to empower each individual and support the diverse cultures, perspectives, skills and experiences within our workforce.

Some Careers Have More Impact Than Others.

If you’re looking for a career where you can make a real impression, join HSBC and discover how valued you’ll be.

We are currently seeking an experienced professional to join our team in the role of Senior Consultant Specialist.

Business:CTO Platforms

Principal Responsibilities

  • Track, monitor, and evidence compliance for key IT controls and KCIs across IDAM, SDLC, Deployment (DEPL), Cyber, Operational Resilience, and other applicable Group control requirements for Group AI Platform Service Management.
  • Own and manage GRAS metrics for the area, ensuring accurate status, clear ownership, and timely progression/closure of actions.Maintain high-quality dashboards, trackers, and reporting packs that provide transparent visibility of compliance status, risks, overdue actions, and upcoming deadlines for senior stakeholders.
  • Drive action management: ensure action owners understand requirements and evidence expectations, follow up regularly, remove blockers, and escalate where actions are at risk or overdue.
  • Represent the function in control governance forums and KCI/control discussions; provide constructive feedback, challenge where needed, and drive favourable outcomes aligned to the Group control framework.
  • Engage regularly with Group IAM, Risk & Control leads, control owners, CCO Tech, Risk Advocates, IT/Business Service Owners, and Service Quality Managers to align expectations and close outstanding items.Prepare and present compliance status, key risks, trends, and mitigation plans for CTO/CIO/SLR and other senior governance forums.
  • Track and ensure timely closure of audit issues/findings/actions related to IT controls, ensuring evidence quality is audit-ready and traceable. Identify and deliver continuous improvement opportunities (process improvements, playbooks, training/awareness sessions) to strengthen control performance and operational discipline.
  • Share IT Service Owner (ITSO) responsibilities for nominated Group AI Platform services, supporting service governance and service health oversight (e.g., incidents/problems awareness, change risk, operational risk management, service reviews).
  • Ensure service documentation remains current and fit for purpose (e.g., service profiles, support models, key contacts, runbooks, DR artefacts) and that control requirements are embedded into service operations.

Requirements

  • Proven experience in IT control compliance tracking, KCI/KPI reporting, and action management in a regulated environment.
  • Strong organisational and stakeholder management skills, with the ability to influence, challenge, and escalate appropriately to drive closure.
  • Working knowledge of Cybersecurity controls, SDLC, deployment/change controls, and Identity & Access Management concepts.
  • Experience producing dashboards and senior management reporting (e.g., Excel/Power BI or equivalent), with strong attention to detail and evidence quality.
  • Experience supporting IT Service Ownership / Service Management activities for critical services (service reviews, operational risk management, and service stability/resilience focus).
  • Excellent verbal and written communication skills, able to communicate effectively with senior IT and business stakeholders. Ability to work independently, take ownership, and drive global functional teams towards common objectives.

You’ll achieve more when you join HSBC.

HSBC is an equal opportunity employer committed to building a culture where all employees are valued, respected and opinions count. We take pride in providing a workplace that fosters continuous professional development, flexible working and, opportunities to grow within an inclusive and diverse environment. We encourage applications from all suitably qualified persons irrespective of, but not limited to, their gender or genetic information, sexual orientation, ethnicity, religion, social status, medical care leave requirements, political affiliation, people with disabilities, color, national origin, veteran status, etc., We consider all applications based on merit and suitability to the role.

Personal data held by the Bank relating to employment applications will be used in accordance with our Privacy Statement, which is available on our website.
